# Results

## *Sasa* expanded by a net +19% over 9 years {#sec-res-change}

The area classified as *Sasa* (geodesic area) increased from 8,542 m² in 2012 to 10,170 m² in 2021, a net change of +1,628 m² (+19%) over 9 years. This net change reflects the difference between gross expansion of 4,095 cells (non-*Sasa*→*Sasa*; 48% of the 2012 area) and gross loss of 2,468 cells (*Sasa*→non-*Sasa*; 29%) (@fig-sasa-change; the full transition matrix is in Table S3). Expansion originated mainly from other vegetation (53%) and dwarf pine (35%), with the three deciduous shrub classes (rowans, maple, and montane alder) together accounting for 12%. Loss was predominantly to dwarf pine (47%) and other vegetation (38%), with the three deciduous shrub classes together accounting for 15%. *Sasa* exchanged area in both directions with every other class; the exchange with dwarf pine was the most nearly balanced between the two directions (interpretation in @sec-disc-change). In the blind interpretation of paired images, 73–87% of loss cells were assigned to boundary ambiguity, a proportion essentially unchanged from that in stable controls (80–85%). Canopy cover was assigned to 8 of the 37 sampled *Sasa*→dwarf pine loss cells (22%), only slightly above the corresponding judgement for stable dwarf pine controls (3 of 20; 15%) (Table S5). A few 2021 *Sasa* cells lay isolated from all 2012 *Sasa* cells; visual inspection of the corresponding image regions confirmed no new isolated patches, so we attribute these cells to classification noise rather than to establishment from seeds.

## Snowmelt timing followed microtopographic gradients, with no detectable trend over 10 years {#sec-res-snow}

The mean snowmelt date ranged from approximately DOY 120 to 230 across the slope, following a ridge-to-hollow gradient (Figure S2). Per-cell trends were negative in 91.7% of cells, positive in 8.3%, and zero in 0.06% (mean −0.71 days/year, median −0.63, SD 0.63; Figure S3), but the annual spatial means varied markedly among years, and the landscape trend was not distinguishable from zero (−0.69 days/year, 95% confidence interval −2.24 to +0.87, p = 0.34; Figure S1). Only 2.0% of cells had individually significant slopes (p < 0.05), and none remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction. Trends are used below only to define projection scenarios (@sec-projection).

## Environmentally suitable area greatly exceeded occupied area (Model A) {#sec-res-modelA}

The main Model A, covering the full elevation range, achieved a held-out TSS of 0.78 (mean across 4 spatial blocks; range 0.72–0.85) and an AUC of 0.95. Four members remained in the LASSO blend: 2 gradient boosted tree models, 1 MaxEnt model, and 1 random forest, with boosted trees and MaxEnt accounting for approximately 97% of the blend weight. Response curves (@fig-response-A) showed high habitat suitability at a mean snowmelt date of approximately DOY 150–185, peaking near DOY 172. Habitat suitability was highest at approximately 2,400–2,550 m, fell sharply above approximately 2,550 m, near the upper limit of the observed distribution, and declined with increasing slope. Responses to TPI, TWI, and aspect components were weaker and non-monotonic. Because estimates of suitable area depend strongly on the binarisation threshold, we primarily used the threshold of 0.16 that maximised TSS on held-out predictions (full threshold sensitivity in Table S8). At this threshold, suitable area was 164×10³ m², approximately 16 times the observed occupied area of 10.2×10³ m². Suitable area consistently exceeded occupied area at thresholds up to 0.55 (@fig-models-AB a).

Grey bands along the bottom of the panels show the distribution (density) of each predictor in presence cells.](files/fig03_response_curves.png){#fig-response-A width=100%}

## Establishment depended strongly on distance from the existing front (Model B) {#sec-res-modelB}

Of the 1,197,536 cells that were non-*Sasa* in 2012, 4,095 had become *Sasa* by 2021. The establishment GAM discriminated well between establishment and non-establishment cells in leave-one-fold-out evaluation (pooled AUC 0.946, TSS 0.75; fold-specific AUC 0.91–0.96). A gradient boosted tree ensemble fitted on the same folds to all establishment cells and a fold-stratified sample of 150,000 non-establishment cells achieved an AUC of 0.948, indicating that the additive model captured nearly all the signal available to a more flexible learner. Distance from the 2012 front was the strongest term. The 9-year establishment probability declined from approximately 10% within 5 m of the front to approximately 1% at 5–10 m and below 0.1% beyond 80 m. Mean fitted establishment probabilities within each distance band closely matched the observed establishment rates throughout the range (@fig-models-AB e; the largest discrepancy was 0.5 percentage points in the 0–5 m band). Environmental associations were consistent with Model A for snowmelt and slope: establishment probability peaked at a mean snowmelt date of approximately DOY 175, declining towards both earlier- and later-melting cells, and declined on steeper slopes. The partial effect of elevation, in contrast, was weak and uncertain within the elevation range of observed establishment (partial effects of all Model B predictors in Figure S8). The map of 9-year establishment probability evaluated from the 2021 front (@fig-models-AB b) was concentrated in narrow bands around existing patches, with the highest values along their lower, late-melting edges.

## Projected establishment continued near existing fronts {#sec-res-projection}

Before projecting beyond the observed period, we checked that the cellular automaton reproduced the observed 2012–2021 change. Initialised from the 2012 distribution, it reproduced the observed gross expansion (expected 4,414 m² versus observed 4,093 m²; ratio 1.08; cell-level AUC 0.92); because Model B was fitted to the same interval, this is a calibration check rather than independent validation. In the independent spatial validation, in which each fold was predicted by a model never exposed to it, AUC ranged from 0.79 to 0.86, whereas fold-level ratios of expected to observed area ranged from 0.67 to 2.0. Discrimination of establishment *location* was thus stable in unseen areas, but prediction errors in the *amount* of establishment were substantial.

Starting from the 2021 distribution, expected establishment area by 2030 was 4,901 m² under the no-change scenario (s = 0; SD across replicates 70) and 5,730 m² under continued snowmelt advance at the observed rate (s = −0.71 days/year; SD 84), the latter 17% greater than the former (@fig-ca-projection). Both trajectories were nearly linear over 9 years, and both were of similar magnitude to the observed 2012–2021 gross expansion (geodesic area 4,093 m²). Establishment probability was highest along the lower, snowbed-facing edges of existing patches and negligible more than a few tens of metres from any patch (@fig-ca-projection a, b). The extreme scenario at the lower confidence limit of the trend (s = −2.24 days/year) yielded 5,524 m², slightly *less* than the point-estimate scenario (Table S11). Projected area was not a monotonic function of earlier snowmelt (mechanism discussed in @sec-disc-drivers). Structural sensitivity of the projections is reported in Table S10; in particular, relaxing the no-loss assumption by removing occupied cells at the annual rate implied by the observed 2012–2021 gross loss reduced expected establishment area by 13% under both reported scenarios.

## Risk of establishment by 2030 was concentrated in two snowbed communities adjoining existing patches {#sec-res-risk}

Within cells classified as other vegetation in 2021, the expected establishment area by 2030 was 2,429 m² (s = 0) and 3,383 m² (s = −0.71 days/year) (@fig-risk a). Overlain on the Ministry of the Environment's 1:25,000 vegetation map, 73–74% of this expected area fell in the *Fauria crista-galli*–*Carex blepharicarpa* snowbed community and a further 15–16% in the *Anaphalis alpicola*–*Phyllodoce aleutica* snowbed community; together, approximately nine tenths of the expected area lay in snowbed vegetation. The remaining tenth was mapped as dwarf pine community (@fig-risk b; Table S12). Observed 2012–2021 establishment had a similar composition (67%, 11%, and 22%, respectively; Table S12). The seed-dispersal stratum, Model A's suitable area within other vegetation in 2021 at the TSS-maximising threshold, was more than an order of magnitude larger (Figure S7).
